subject: Close readout: units/$ validation and gating criteria for Pilot MAP
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: samira@clearwavehealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Close readout: units/$ validation and gating criteria for Pilot MAP

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, here’s a concise readout of the unit-econ checks we want to lock down as part of the Pilot MAP before we move to the contract signature milestone. I attached a draft MAP and a small workbook that runs the tokens/$ sensitivity table that underpins the acceptance criteria. Key items below — please review and confirm whether the traffic profile below matches ClearWave’s expectations.

Top-line assumptions (for the Pilot):
- Traffic profile: 12k API calls/day with 1.9 average user-turns/session (median), burst to 2.5x during peak windows.
- Typical prompt + response: median 230 tokens (prompt 80 / completion 150).
- Target KV/prefix cache hit: 50% (templated dialogs & clinical snippets).
- Recommended batching window: 20 ms for low-latency routes; up to 75 ms for background/async routes.
- Quantization: 8-bit production variant for the hosted test.

What we need to validate in the MAP (acceptance / gating criteria):
1) Units-per-dollar sanity check: final tokens/$ range validated in workbook and signed off by ClearWave finance. We want agreement on the nominal tokens/$ we’ll use for invoicing scenarios and a +/- tolerance for close decisions.
2) Cache effect confirmation: confirm expected cacheable fraction of prompts (we used 45–60% range). If ClearWave expects <30% cacheability, we need to re-run the token-econ model with lower hit rates.
3) Latency SLO vs batching trade: identify which API endpoints can accept 50–75 ms batching vs which must stay <=20 ms. This determines the effective token throughput and cost.
4) Eval plan linkage: pick 5 canonical prompts (we suggested clinical triage, med-sum, deferral reasons) to monitor regression and token volatility across model variants.
5) Security/compliance redlines that would materially change cost (e.g., on-prem/private deployment requirement, additional KMS usage).

Immediate asks for ClearWave:
- Confirm the daily call profile and the percentage of highly templated dialogs (estimate).
- Sign off on the 5 eval prompts or propose replacements.
- Procurement: flag any billing cadence or PO constraints that change invoicing assumptions.

I’ll coordinate a short follow-up workshop once you confirm the prompts and traffic profile — we’ll run two quick simulations (baseline + conservative cache case) and push the updated workbook to the Drive link above.

Attachments: ClearWave_MAP_v1.2.pdf (MAP draft), token-econ-workbook.xlsx (calc tab + sensitivity).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Close readout: units/$ validation and gating criteria for Pilot MAP

Laura —

Appreciate the level of detail. A few clarifying items from our side before we book the workshop:

1) Tokens: does the workbook count system prompts and assistant tokens in the tokens/$ estimate? Our current internal tracking excludes template system tokens (we only bill user+assistant body).
2) PHI & caching: caching templated turns is appealing, but we need to confirm whether cached prefix results will retain PHI. Is Redwood’s hosted cache encrypted at rest and what is the default TTL? Any impact to cost if we need to limit caching for PHI endpoints?
3) Batching: procurement wants a short note on worst-case latency impact for single-turn clinical flows if batching is increased to 50–75 ms (they want to ensure observable UX regressions are minimal).
4) Procurement: please confirm invoicing cadence (monthly) and whether there’s a minimum commit period for the Pilot MAP credits. We’d also like a one-line on credit/overage handling.

Also — quick ask: can you include a worked example showing tokens/$ for a 1M-token month with both cache ON (50% hit) and cache OFF? That will help our finance team compare to internal forecasts.

Samira
Samira Patel

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Hi Samira —

Quick technical clarifications to help with the workbook example below (copying Laura):

- Tokens counted: our standard workbook includes user + assistant tokens. System prompt tokens are shown separately in the calc sheet (row: system_tokens) so you can easily exclude them for your internal comparison. I’ll attach a pared-down calc in the Drive.

- Caching & PHI: Redwood’s hosted KV/prefix cache is encrypted at rest and access-controlled. Default TTL is 15 minutes for the Pilot template, configurable by route. If you need PHI-isolated behavior, we can mark routes as non-cacheable or route them to Private deployment (that will change unit economics — see note).

- Worked example (high level):
  * Baseline compute assumptions we used in the workbook: 8-bit quantized variant, effective cost per token (compute + infra) ≈ $0.0000065/token -> ~153k tokens per $1.
  * For 1,000,000 tokens/month:
    - Cache OFF: 1,000,000 tokens -> cost ≈ $6.50 (compute/inference only, excludes storage/observability e.g., metrics retention).
    - Cache ON (50% hit): effective billable tokens ≈ 500,000 -> cost ≈ $3.25.
  * If you require Private deployment (on-prem/VPC) for PHI: we model an uplift (fixed infra amortization + network) that increases effective cost to roughly $0.000021/token -> ~47k tokens/$1. That scenario is included as a toggled sheet in the workbook.

- Batching & latency: raising batching window from 20ms to 75ms increases throughput and reduces per-token cost (fewer dispatch cycles), but increases tail latency for single-turn calls. In our internal tests, user-perceived latency increases by ~10–40 ms on tails depending on request size. For clinical single-turn flows we recommend keeping 20 ms. Background/async labeling is safe for 50–75 ms batching.

I’ll update the Drive workbook with the 1M-token worked examples and a separate sheet modeling the Private deployment uplift.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samira / Procurement team —

Thanks for the questions; Karthik’s numbers are now in the workbook (Drive link above). I summarized next steps and the MAP gating items below so we have agreement and a short timeline to close:

Mutual Action Plan (next milestones) — summary and owners
- A: Confirm traffic profile & templated-turn % (ClearWave) — due Thu, Jul 26. Owner: Samira.
- B: Review & sign the 5 eval prompts (ClearWave) — due Fri, Jul 28. Owner: Samira / Clinical SME.
- C: Redwood to run two sims (baseline, conservative cache-off) and publish a final tokens/$ sensitivity sheet — due Mon, Jul 31. Owner: Karthik + Laura.
- D: Procurement to confirm invoicing cadence & PO requirements (ClearWave) — due Mon, Jul 31. Owner: procurement@clearwavehealth.com
- E: Sign-off on MAP and issue initial Pilot PO or credit commitment — target Thu, Aug 3. Owner: Samira + Procurement + Redwood Sales.

Acceptance criteria (for Pilot close):
1) Tokens/$ workbook shows a bounded tokens/$ range agreed by both parties (nominal +/- 15%).
2) Cacheable-turn confirmation >= 40% OR agreement to run a conservative (cache-off) plan with adjusted economics.
3) Latency-sensitive endpoints identified and configured with <=20 ms batching.
4) Security check: if ClearWave allows hosted cache for templated turns (encrypted at rest), no Private deployment required for Pilot. If they require Private, we’ll re-baseline and present updated pricing within 48 hours.

Procurement note (one-line we can use for PO): monthly invoicing based on billable tokens (user+assistant tokens) with overage billed at the agreed tokens/$ rate; Pilot minimum term = 30 days; any prepayment/credit will be applied against usage. If procurement needs exact contract language, I can loop in legal and send a one-page SOW.

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule the 45-minute workshop during the week of Jul 30 to run the sims and walk the finance folks through the workbook calculations.

Thanks —
Laura
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
